updateCadence: Irregular; tracks selected Chromium releases (144 through June-July 2026, 150 by Oct 2026) with R-revisions
summary: A Chromium fork that keeps current Blink/V8 running on Windows XP through 11, with Google Sync, Chrome Web Store access and ungoogled-chromium privacy flags. The only mainstream way to get a recent Chromium engine on XP/Vista/7.
bestFor: Old PCs needing a modern engine
People wanting MV2 uBlock Origin on a Chromium base
notFor: Users on current Windows who want fast security patching
Anyone needing macOS, Linux or mobile

pros.title: Runs on XP to 11
pros.detail: Windows XP SP1+, Vista, 7, 8, 10, 11 in 32-bit and 64-bit builds.

pros.title: Modern engine on old OS
pros.detail: Tracks current Chromium major versions, so most modern sites work where Firefox ESR or old Chrome fail.

pros.title: Sync works on XP
pros.detail: Google Sync is functional even on Windows XP per Wikipedia.

pros.title: MV2 kept
pros.detail: Project says MV2 is not slated for removal and uBlock Origin can be sideloaded from GitHub.

pros.title: Light on old hardware
pros.detail: Runs from 768 MB RAM with SSE2 or SSE3 CPUs.

cons.title: Windows only
cons.detail: No macOS, Linux or mobile builds.

cons.title: Security on legacy OS
cons.detail: XP/Vista lack modern OS mitigations; sandbox strength is below Chrome on Windows 11.

cons.title: Patch lag
cons.detail: Supermium 150 is months behind current stable Chrome; patch cadence depends on one developer.

cons.title: Rough edges
cons.detail: Occasional process failures on some XP systems were still open in Oct 2026.

faq.q: Does Supermium work on Windows XP in 2026?
faq.a: Yes. Windows XP SP3 or later with a Pentium 4+ SSE2 CPU and at least 768 MB RAM; release 150 notes still list an open XP process-failure fix.
MV2 extensions work by sideloading per the project; Wikipedia says MV2 is not yet available, so this is contested.

faq.q: Is it safe to use on XP?
faq.a: The browser engine is current-ish, but the OS itself is unpatched, so risk remains.

timeline.event: Version 119 adds Vista support without Extended Kernel

spec.codecs: H.264, VP9, AV1 (software on old hardware)

graphics: Software/D3D9 paths on old OS; no WebGPU yet
lowEnd: Only modern Chromium that installs on XP/Vista/7; 768 MB RAM minimum
securityHardening: Chromium sandbox but XP/Vista OS lacks modern mitigations
patchSpeed: Chromium 150 R2 in Oct 2026 while stable Chrome is ~156; one developer
extensions: Chrome Web Store plus sideloaded MV2 uBO
sync: Google Sync works, even on XP
webCompat: Modern Blink; some GPU/OS features missing on XP

unverified: Whether MV2 is natively supported or only sideloadable (Wikipedia vs project site disagree)
Release date discrepancy: Gizmodo lists 150.0.7871.255 R2 as 2026-10-09, search summary says 2026-10-21 for R2.01
